chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Abu Sa'id al-Makari said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog that is sent out for hunting, and it says the name of God, then it kills and eats from the prey; he said: 'Eat, even if it eats from it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat if the hunting dog eats some of it before you do?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the consumption of game hunted by a trained dog remains permissible even if the dog eats from the prey, provided the hunter recites the name of God upon sending it. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the dog's eating does not render the meat impure or invalid, distinguishing it from other conditions of hunting. The hadith underscores the practical ease granted to believers in acquiring lawful sustenance through animal labor.
